newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Rio's transvestites charm carnival crowds.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Rio's transvestites charm carnival crowds.

text.p: Festive transvestites defied police threats on Saturday as they mocked the nation's armed forces in beachfront Carnival parades through Rio's elegant Impanema neighbourhood.
Police had said they would arrest anyone who ridiculed the military, but marchers prancing in uniforms complemented by fishnet stockings and pleated mini-skirts were not bothered.
The transvestite parades were the highlight of the second day of the festival of debauchery that celebrates the final days before the beginning of Lent.

Each year, Carnival builds over the weekend to explode in a blaze of colours and sequined glitter on Sunday and Monday nights when the special-group schools stage their dusk- to-dawn parades with ornate floats and extravagant costumes.
Several thousand dancers from schools with million-dollar budgets often bankrolled by Rio's organised crime bosses compete fiercely to become Carnival champions.

On Saturday, thousands lined the beachfronts to watch marchers who included a pink-garbed Cinderella armed with an oversized condom searching for her Prince Charming, a group of five cows in fishnet stockings and huge platform shoes, a pair of rhinestone cowgirls and other beauties.
Revellers were not worried about the police as they guzzled beer and danced in the streets.

"This is carnival. We are here to play and have fun, not to offend anyone," said Karylia, who would not reveal his real name. "This is not the time to make any statements. We are just doing what we do every year."
"I don't think they will really arrest us, but if they do I'll worry about it when they come," he added.
Relations between Brazil's gay community and the armed forces are strained, and rights groups are fighting discrimination against gays in the military.
Meanwhile, the best of the lower-rank samba schools kicked off the second day of parades at Rio's sambadrome stadium in the hope of gaining a place among the city's elite of samba schools.
Rio's world famous Carnival celebrations were officially opened on Friday by this year's Rei Momo or carnival Fat King, who weighed in at an impressive 475 pounds (215 kg).
In a ceremony in the city centre, the mayor of Rio handed the monarch a huge symbolic key to the city so he could unleash the four-day revelry.

Carnival organisers expected the 70,000-capacity sambadrome to be packed to the last seat on both Sunday and Monday nights, with spectators from all over the world admiring the glamorous procession of some 60,000 samba dancers.
